conviction_note: Q3 is a fresh (not pre-released) quarter whose real line is whether the FY26 guide (adj. EBITDA EUR 500-530m) is held. Company numbers put the run-rate near or below the low end, while the company-compiled consensus (FY 509, Q3 130.3) sits above that. Against that: no MAR ad-hoc guidance cut in the six weeks since the quarter closed (and a buyback ad-hoc was filed on 5 Nov), a EUR 2 dividend floor that makes an EBITDA/FCF trim matter less to holders, and a stock that rose after the Q1 and H1 misses. So abs_move is 4.0 (fresh numbers, roughly a 30% chance of a low-end or trim message) with p_up 47, giving -0.24. The findings sum to -0.6, and the gap between the two numbers is the reaction function pulling p_up toward 50.

findings.finding: On the company's own numbers the FY26 run-rate sits at or below the low end of the 500-530m adj. EBITDA guide, while the company-compiled consensus sits at 509. Quarterly yoy deltas were -4.6m in Q1 and -10.7m in Q2. Q4 2025 (120.3m) already carried the ~13m MNO charge, and the FY26 MNO hit of ~50m leaves ~28m for H2. Carried forward, that gives FY ~490-500, and consensus implies a Q4 of ~136m, about 16m above Q4 2025 and close to the Q4 2025 underlying of ~133m before this year's ~14m Q4 MNO hit.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The FY25 print with the first 2026 guide (below expectations, 25 Feb 2026 18:00) moved -13.94% the next session. Q1 (15 May) and H1 (12 Aug) confirmed the guide despite EBITDA misses and moved +3.89% and +1.44%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus (09.10.2026, range 506-514 on FY) still assumes an H2 roughly 25m stronger than H1. A market that had priced a low-end outcome would show estimates sitting at or below 500. The stock is near its lows (52-week low ~21.7 in October), so part of it is in the price, and the +4.8% 5-day run-up into the print does not look like a market braced for a trim. This is an inference from public numbers that any analyst could make, so it is sized well below the -9% guidance-change base.

Against it: there has been no MAR ad-hoc Prognosesenkung since the quarter closed, although the company filed an ad-hoc on 5 Nov.

findings.finding: Capital return and portfolio moves just before the print: an ad-hoc EUR 75m buyback (about 2.7% of market cap at EUR 23.7) funded from ~EUR 150m of Ceconomy proceeds, plus the ~EUR 76m buyout of waipu.tv minorities at an EV of ~EUR 300m, which takes all IPTV cash flow in-house. The buyback's start date and volume are still to be set and could be specified with the release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Buyback ad-hoc (5 Nov 20:37) was followed by +0.43% on 6 Nov. The waipu buyout (13 Oct 18:00) was followed by +0.90% and +1.97% over the next two sessions.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: both items are public and the stock has risen 4.8% over five sessions. What is left is the start of buying inside the window, if the release names a start date, and the fact that the EUR 2 dividend floor now comes with buyback support. Any dividend-floor doubt priced into an ~8.5% yield would ease if a start is named.

Any relief disclosed in the release would be upside to both the guide and the 2028 ambition.

findings.why_not_priced: There is no sign of a deal: neither the H1 release nor any news through 10 Nov reports one, and H1 still reads 'ongoing dialogue'. The probability of an announcement in this release is low, so the finding is sized small with a long right tail. If a deal were expected, consensus FY Mobile would sit above the guide midpoint and not at 392.

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed history of freenet trading on a network operator's print.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and only a proxy. Telekom's branded growth can come partly at service providers' expense, so the sign carries through to freenet weakly. Sized near zero.

baseline_tension: The evidence leans mildly against the baseline's positive priced lean (+1.44, mostly a borrowed short-squeeze prior on a flat 3% short) and against the +4.8% 5-day run-up. The negative rests on inference from public numbers, while the reaction history (misses bought at Q1 and H1) and the absence of an ad-hoc cut both pull toward 50. So p_up sits at 47, only just below 50.
language_note: Börsen-Zeitung (German) carried the CFO's explicit 'im schlechtesten Fall ... 50 Mill. Euro ... in unserer Guidance bereits berücksichtigt', names the counterparty as Telefonica Deutschland, and gives the Mobile guide of 390-420m. None of this is in freenet's English releases, which say only 'a mobile network operator'.

Der Aktionär (German) carried the CFO's 'Effekt zwischen null und 50 Millionen Euro', the worst-case framing of the guide, and the ex-dividend explanation of the 14 May -6.46% that the baseline's estimated history mislabels.
4investors (German) gave the 4 Nov +3.1% move its context (technical break of the 50-day line on volume about 70% above average) where the English sources had nothing.
lessons_applied: 'The move is in the guide' (guidance change median 9.0% against 2.3% when reiterated) and 'too small about the move': abs_move_pct 3.5 -> 4.0, since a lower-end or trim message has roughly a 30% chance; the guidance finding -1.2 -> -1.5 with its low end widened to -7.
A reaction history of bought misses moved p_up, not abs_move: p_up kept at 47.
'A German ad-hoc may have pre-released the number': checked, none filed; this is the reason the guidance finding stays an inference and not a call.
'Two findings on one document are one': the Mobile-miss and guidance run-rate items were already merged; nothing further changed.
